questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'REPUDIATE':
questions.explanation: A is correct. Repudiate = to refuse to accept or be associated with; to deny the truth or authority of something. Example: 'The politician repudiated the allegations of corruption.' Synonyms: disown, disavow, reject, denounce.

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'EPHEMERAL':
questions.explanation: D is correct. Ephemeral = lasting for a very short time; transient. From Greek 'epi' (upon) + 'hemera' (day) — lasting only one day. Example: 'Fame can be ephemeral — here today, forgotten tomorrow.' Antonym: permanent, enduring.

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'MAGNANIMOUS':

options.option_text: Generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival

questions.explanation: C is correct. Magnanimous = nobly generous; showing great generosity of spirit, especially to an enemy or defeated rival. Example: 'The victorious team was magnanimous in victory, praising their opponents.' From Latin 'magnus' (great) + 'animus' (soul). Antonym: petty, vindictive.

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'ALACRITY':
questions.explanation: C is correct. Alacrity = liveliness and eagerness; prompt and cheerful willingness. Example: 'She accepted the challenge with alacrity, diving into the work immediately.' Synonyms: eagerness, promptness, zeal, enthusiasm. Antonym: reluctance, sluggishness.

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'LACONIC':
questions.explanation: A is correct. Laconic = using very few words; brief. From Laconia (ancient Sparta) — Spartans were famous for terse communication. Example: 'His laconic reply of just two words left everyone puzzled.' Synonyms: terse, succinct, pithy. Antonym: verbose, loquacious, garrulous.

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'RECALCITRANT':

options.option_text: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control

questions.explanation: D is correct. Recalcitrant = uncooperative; obstinately resistant to instruction or authority. Example: 'The recalcitrant student refused to follow school rules despite multiple warnings.' Synonyms: defiant, unruly, intractable, obstinate. Antonym: compliant, cooperative.

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'OBSEQUIOUS':

options.option_text: Excessively eager to serve or please; fawning

questions.explanation: B is correct. Obsequious = servilely compliant; overly attentive and flattering in a way that appears insincere. Example: 'His obsequious behaviour toward the boss irritated his colleagues.' Synonyms: sycophantic, fawning, servile, toadying. Antonym: assertive, independent.

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'IMPEDE':

options.option_text: To delay or obstruct the progress of

questions.explanation: C is correct. Impede = to obstruct or delay the progress of someone or something. Example: 'The roadblock impeded the emergency vehicle's access to the hospital.' Synonyms: hinder, obstruct, hamper, block, thwart. Antonym: facilitate, aid, expedite.

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to 'PUGNACIOUS':
questions.explanation: A is correct. Pugnacious = eager to argue or fight; combative. From Latin 'pugnare' (to fight). Example: 'His pugnacious personality made negotiations difficult.' Synonyms: belligerent, combative, contentious, quarrelsome. Antonym: peaceful, pacifist, conciliatory.
